prompt: A black and white photograph, shot on 35mm monochrome film stock with visible grain, of a young man lying on a bench press in a cheap, cramped municipal gym in an English industrial town, looking straight up at the older man spotting him. The young man, Brandon, is about 22, with big sticking-out ears, a bad home-cut haircut flattened on one side, a soft pale face and a trusting, open expression; he wears a baggy tracksuit top zipped right up to his neck, like a boy dressed in his dad's idea of smart, and plain cotton trousers. His hands grip a heavy iron barbell loaded with dull, chipped cast-iron plates, held steady above his chest. Standing over him at the head of the bench is Gary, a tired man of about fifty with a heavy brow, a broken nose and deep creases under his eyes, wearing a thick wool donkey jacket over a grey sweatshirt and baggy gym shorts, both hands cupped under the bar, looking down at Brandon with a flat, unreadable gaze. Both faces are clearly visible and lit. The room is a bare brick-walled basement with a painted-over window high up, a worn rubber floor, a rusting rack of dumbbells and a pair of old leather-covered benches with split seams, with no readable text anywhere. The light is hard and practical: a single bare bulb in a metal shade directly above the bench throws a harsh pool of light and deep shadows under brows and chins, while a dim grey overcast daylight seeps in from the high window. Wide framing from a slightly low angle with a 35mm lens, the whole bench, both men and the room around them in the frame, deep focus, ordinary working-class faces with real skin texture, pores, stubble and tired eyes, clothes worn thin and creased. Thanks.
